page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, using the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled. Cache allocation consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning is high relative to compute capacity, delivering 64.0 GB of RAM (32.0 GB per vCPU). Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via a bundled 322 GB SSD, while hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate typical constrained compute performance driven by the 2 vCPU and single physical core allocation. Single-threaded metrics land in the average range, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1631.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1891.2, and single-threaded gzip compression at 28.52 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks rank in the lower percentiles: Geekbench multi-core registers at 1882.0, PassMark CPU score at 2989.31, and stress-ng multi-core at 1934.59. Memory throughput measures 103.85 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read blocks and 14.76 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads, alongside a 2051.42 PassMark memory score.

Operating with an extreme 32 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, the E8-2ds_v5 optimizes hardware expenditures for database and software licensing tiers billed per core. The constraint of a single physical core introduces a performance tradeoff for parallel execution pipelines, compilation tasks, and compute-heavy batch processing. The instance fits memory-heavy, low-parallelism workloads such as enterprise caching layers, constrained database engines requiring large buffer pools, and in-memory analytics systems needing integrated local scratch storage.
